extracted.intended_audience: researchers, funding-agency staff, peer reviewers, and science policy analysts
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and evaluative standards used in peer review of grant proposals, and empirical findings about their performance. Includes common reviewer dimensions, system-level quality metrics, and recommended reforms to improve allocation decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific quality / originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the scientific quality or originality of the research question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a standard reviewer consideration in many systems; Wessely highlights this as one of the core dimensions reviewers are typically asked to evaluate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research approach / methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriateness and rigor of the proposed research approach and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commonly solicited from reviewers as an appraisal of methodological soundness and whether the design will answer the question posed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant track record / qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the investigator's previous productivity, expertise, and suitability to carry out the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to judge likelihood of successful execution; Wessely notes this is a standard axis in historical rubrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility (time/budget)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the proposed work is feasible within the requested time-frame and resources/budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are typically asked to judge whether the plan is realistic and achievable given the constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance of expected results
rubrics_metrics.description: The anticipated importance or impact of the project's results for the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A core dimension in many rubrics—used to assess potential return on investment for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources / institutional environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequacy of institutional support, facilities, and resources available to conduct the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates whether the environment will materially contribute to project success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the scope of work justifies the requested budget (value-for-money).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in lists of reviewer considerations; informs prioritization when budgets are constrained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-reviewer reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of agreement between reviewers on scores and assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wessely synthesizes evidence showing inter-reviewer reliability is low; implies caution in over-interpreting small score differences and suggests need for system changes to improve consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictive validity of review scores
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which reviewer scores predict subsequent researcher productivity or scientific outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical evidence summarized by Wessely indicates reviewer scores have weak predictive validity, so reliance solely on scores to predict future success is questionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias monitoring and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence and impact of systematic biases (e.g., gender) in review outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wessely notes bias is sometimes documented but inconsistent across studies; recommends auditing bias variables and being aware that different systems may show different patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservatism / risk aversion in funding decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Tendency of peer review to favor safe, incremental proposals and disadvantage high-risk/high-reward work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wessely finds conservatism dominates; this suggests rubrics or processes should explicitly account for risk tolerance to avoid systematic under-funding of innovative proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative and time costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Total time and effort required from applicants and reviewers to prepare, submit, and evaluate proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wessely highlights massive time costs; implication is to reduce proposal length/preparation burden and simplify review requirements to lower transaction costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical evidence base for alternative procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of experimental or comparative tests of alternative review procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wessely notes few experimental tests had been conducted to that date; recommends more comparative studies (e.g., forced-ranking vs absolute scoring) to inform reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of lottery elements for borderline proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Introducing random allocation (a lottery) among proposals in the fundable/borderline zone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested reform to acknowledge low discrimination/reliability near funding cutoffs and to reduce bias and wasted reviewer effort; Wessely endorses this as a potential procedural innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit risk-tolerance criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy or rubric elements that state how risk (and potential high reward) should be weighted in review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended by Wessely to counteract conservatism; could be implemented by scoring rubrics or separate funding streams for high-risk work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit of bias variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic monitoring and auditing of review outcomes for demographic or other biases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wessely endorses auditing bias variables as a reform to detect and address inequities across review systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction in proposal length / preparation burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy aim to shorten proposal formats to lower applicant and reviewer time costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wessely recommends reducing paperwork and preparation time as a way to improve system efficiency and reduce wasted effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative (forced-ranking) vs absolute scoring schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference for more relative ranking methods (forced choice/ranking) and fewer absolute scoring frameworks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wessely suggests more comparative approaches may improve discrimination and efficiency; implies reformers should pilot and evaluate forced-ranking systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution about trusting the standard rubric
rubrics_metrics.description: The conventional rubric (significance/approach/PI/feasibility) was judged by Wessely to be too unreliable in its then-current implementation to be fully trusted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a design principle: standard dimensions are necessary but not sufficient—attention must be paid to how they are operationalized, the scoring system, reviewer training, and structural reforms to improve reliability and validity.
